info.title: SalesBlink API
info.description:
SalesBlink Public API Documentation

## Get Your API Key

Get your API Key here: https://run.salesblink.io/account/integration/api

## Authentication

All API endpoints require an API Key passed in the `Authorization` header:
```
Authorization: your_salesblink_api_key
```

## Base URL
- `https://run.salesblink.io/api/public/v1.0.0`

## Core Concepts

The API is organized around a small set of objects. Endpoints are grouped under these names in the sidebar, shown in brackets below.

### Building a campaign

- **Workspace** — The top-level container that owns everything else: senders, lists, leads, sequences, templates, folders and users. "Workspace" and "account" are the same object. A user can belong to several workspaces, each with its own permission, but an API key is tied to exactly one workspace and can only see that workspace's data — to work in another workspace, use a key from that workspace. Only owners can list workspaces. [Workspaces, Account]
- **Lead** — One person you are reaching out to: email address, first and last name, company, phone, plus any custom fields you define. A lead belongs to one list and can be moved to another; the same person may exist in more than one list. "Lead" and "Contact" are the same object — older endpoints use `/contacts`, newer ones use `/leads`. [Leads]
- **List** — A named collection of leads, and the unit you attach to a sequence. A list also carries email-verification and duplicate-removal settings, and counts of its valid, risky and invalid contacts. [Lists]
- **Template** — A reusable email — subject line, body and up to three attachments — with personalization variables such as `{{first_name}}` and `{{company}}`. Every template is returned with a `cold_email_score` computed from its content. A sequence's email steps reference a template rather than holding their own content. [Templates]
- **Sequence** — An automated, multi-step outreach campaign. A sequence is an ordered flow of **steps**: an *email* step (which references a template) or a *delay* step (wait N days). It runs against one or more lists and sends through selected senders. A sequence can start immediately or be scheduled, and can then be started, paused, stopped, cloned, exported or archived. [Sequences]
- **Sender** — A connected mailbox that SalesBlink sends from and receives replies into: Gmail / Google Workspace, Outlook / Microsoft 365, or a custom SMTP + IMAP account. Each sender carries its own daily sending limit and ramp-up settings, warmup settings, signature, optional tracking domain and health score. Sequences always send through senders. Google and Outlook senders are connected through an OAuth flow. [Senders, OAuth]
- **Folder** — A grouping used to keep things tidy. *General* folders organize lists, templates and sequences; *email-sender* folders (`type: email-sender`) organize senders only. [Folders]

### Deliverability

- **Warmup** — Automated email sent back and forth between mailboxes, with replies, opens and read behaviour simulated, to build a sender's reputation before and during real outreach. It is enabled per sender and has its own daily frequency, which can ramp up automatically to a ceiling, plus its own schedule and stats. [Senders, Warmup]
- **Warmup link** — A saved URL with a display label. Senders can be given a set of warmup links, which are then inserted as ordinary-looking anchors into the warmup emails they send. [Warmup]
- **Sender health** — A 0–100 reputation score for a single sender, reported alongside its connection, sending, receiving and warmup state. A sender can be configured to pause cold emails automatically when its score falls below a threshold. [Senders]
- **Inbox placement test** — A deliverability test that sends a message to a set of seed mailboxes across providers and reports where each copy landed, summarized as inbox / spam / promotions / updates / other / not received. The message can be custom or taken from a sequence or template, sent either through your connected senders (`from-salesblink`) or from a mailbox outside SalesBlink (`from-outside`), one-time or on a recurring weekly schedule. Each run also records a domain blacklist check and a SpamAssassin score. [Inbox Placement]
- **Custom domain** — A domain you own and have verified in the workspace, used in place of a shared SalesBlink domain — as a click/open tracking domain on a sender, or as a meeting-link domain. The same section also searches for new `.com` domains available to buy. [Domains]
- **Signature** — A saved HTML email signature that can be attached to a sender and appended to outgoing mail. [Signatures]
- **Blocklist** — A suppression list of email addresses and whole domains. Before each send, both the recipient's address and its domain are checked against it, and a match stops the email. Recipients who unsubscribe are added automatically; you can also add, check and remove entries yourself. The list is scoped to the user the API key belongs to, not shared across the whole workspace. [Blocklist]
- **DFY (Done-For-You)** — A managed order in which SalesBlink buys domains and sets up ready-to-use mailboxes on your behalf. Orders and their mailboxes can be listed through the API; placing an order, adding a mailbox or cancelling one is done in the web UI through a login link. [DFY]

### Results

- **Inbox** — The unified inbox: messages received across all connected senders, grouped into threads. You can read a thread, reply to or forward a message, mark it read or unread, and label a conversation's outcome as positive, negative or neutral. [Inbox]
- **Activity** — The raw, per-email event log — one record per event, with the time, sequence, recipient and message. `/sent`, `/opens`, `/clicks` and `/replies` are four fixed views of that log. [Activity]
- **Reports** — The same event log, with filters left open: by type, sequence, node (step or template), recipient email, sender or log message. [Reports]
- **Sequence stats** — Totals for a single sequence across its full history and all its senders: leads, sent, scheduled, pending, outbox, opens, clicks, replies, bounces, unsubscribes, positive replies and errors. [Sequence Stats]
- **Analytics** — The same events aggregated rather than listed: overall, day by day, per lead, or per mailbox. [Analytics]

### Access

- **User** — A team member inside a workspace. A user's permission in that workspace — owner, admin, client, user or developer — decides what they can see and do; only owners and admins can invite new users. [Users]
- **API key** — The credential you pass in the `Authorization` header. A key belongs to one user in one workspace and inherits that user's permission. Keys can be listed and deleted through the API; creating or refreshing one is done in the web UI. [API Keys, Account]
- **Login link** — A short-lived magic link (valid 1–30 minutes) that drops the user straight into a specific page of the SalesBlink app without a password. It is how the API hands off actions that must be completed in the UI: billing, connecting senders, managing API keys and DFY orders. Note that the sign-up link under Authentication is not one of these — it is just the public sign-up URL. [Users, Billing, Senders, API Keys, DFY, Authentication]

## Rate Limits

The SalesBlink API implements tiered rate limiting based on request type:

| Tier | Limit | Applies To |
|------|-------|------------|
| **General** | 30 requests per minute | GET requests |
| **Sensitive** | 15 requests per minute | POST and PATCH requests |
| **Restricted** | 10 requests per minute | PUT and DELETE requests |

### Requesting Rate Limit Increases

Need higher limits? Contact us at https://salesblink.io/contact-us to discuss your requirements.

## Support
For support, contact: https://salesblink.io/contact-us

Note: only `type`, `sequence`, `search`, `date`, `sender`, `limit`, and `skip` are actually applied by the API. The `days`, `unread`, `starred`, `archived`, and `owned_by` parameters are accepted for compatibility but currently have no effect. Omit `type` to get replies (the default).

post.description:
Send a reply to a lead's email. The reply will be sent from the same sender that originally contacted the lead.
Conversation continuity is maintained automatically. Optional `scheduled_time`, `tzMode` and `selectedTimezone` can be used to schedule the reply.

scheduled_time.description: Unix timestamp in ms to schedule the reply. If omitted or in the past, the reply is sent after a short delay.

tzMode.description: Timezone mode. 'sequence' uses the sequence timezone, 'custom' uses selectedTimezone.

selectedTimezone.description: IANA timezone to use when tzMode is 'custom'.

patch.description:
Update the state of an inbox item. The underlying controller applies any body fields directly to the task document, so fields beyond `unread` and `outcome` may be accepted; only documented fields are guaranteed to behave predictably.
The `unread` field marks read/unread status and the `outcome` field classifies replies (e.g., positive, negative, neutral).

outcome.description: Set conversation outcome (e.g., positive, negative, neutral)

content.description: Optional additional message content (defaults to the original email body)

tzMode.description: Timezone mode. 'sequence' uses the sequence timezone, 'custom' uses selectedTimezone.

selectedTimezone.description: IANA timezone to use when tzMode is 'custom'.

post.description:
Create a new automated email sequence.

- The steps array defines the sequence flow with email and delay nodes.
- Each email step requires a template_id
- Each delay step requires days (number of days to wait)
- If launchTimingMode is not provided or 'now', sequence starts 5 minutes from now
- If 'schedule', provide scheduledAt as a future UTC timestamp in milliseconds. ISO 8601 datetime strings with timezone offset are documented but are not parsed correctly by the current API.
- When scheduling, always provide the user's timezone in the timezone field (e.g. 'Asia/Calcutta') so the sequence does not default to America/New_York

senders.description: Comma-separated sender/folder UUIDs. Can include both sender IDs and folder IDs. Folder IDs here must be email-sender folders.

lists.description: Array of list UUIDs to include (required)

steps.description: Ordered array of sequence steps (required). Mix of email and delay steps

folder.description: Optional general folder ID to organize the sequence. Must be a folder created without a type (i.e., not an email-sender folder).

launchTimingMode.description: When to launch: 'now' (default, starts in 5 mins) or 'schedule' (requires scheduledAt and timezone)

scheduledAt.description: Launch time (required if launchTimingMode=schedule, must be future). UTC timestamp in milliseconds is recommended. ISO 8601 datetime strings with timezone offset are not parsed correctly by the current API.

timezone.description: IANA timezone for scheduled sending (e.g. 'Asia/Calcutta', 'America/New_York'). Required when launchTimingMode=schedule to avoid defaulting to America/New_York.

paused.description: Whether to create the sequence in paused state (default true)

autoPause.description: Enable auto-pause on high bounce rate

emailSendingHours.description: Configure sending hours for each day of the week. Must contain one entry for every day (Monday-Sunday). Each entry needs enabled, name, fromTime and toTime.

validEmail.description: Send to contacts with valid email status

riskyEmail.description: Send to contacts with risky email status

invalidEmail.description: Send to contacts with invalid email status

checkEmailOpen.description: Check if recipient opened previous email before sending next

checkEmailClick.description: Check if recipient clicked link before sending next

checkEmailReply.description: Check if recipient replied before sending next

matchProvider.description: Match sender email provider with recipient

stopWhenReplyRecievedWhen.description: When to stop sequence on reply

bcc.description: BCC email address for all outgoing emails

message.description: If checkEmailBeforeSending is true, this instead reads 'Sequence created successfully. You will need to approve emails manually from the outbox before they are sent.'

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the sequence

post.description:
Upload a CSV file containing multiple email senders.

### Supported CSV Columns

- **Required**: `from_email`, `password`, `smtp_host`, `smtp_port`
- **Core**: `from_name`, `user_name`
- **IMAP**: `imap_host`, `imap_port`, `imap_user_name`, `imap_password`
- **Warmup**: `warmup_enabled`, `warmup_auto_ramp_up_enabled`, `warmup_initial_daily_frequency`, `warmup_ramp_up_frequency`, `warmup_max_daily_frequency`, `warmup_tag`, `inbox_enable`, `inbox_path`, `spam_path`, `pause_cold_emails_when_health_low`, `pause_cold_emails_health_threshold`
- **Sequence**: `sequence_auto_ramp_up_enabled`, `sequence_initial_daily_frequency`, `sequence_ramp_up_frequency`, `sequence_max_daily_frequency` (or `max_emails_per_day`)
- **Other**: `signature_id`, `custom_tracking_url`, `dkim_identifier`, `reply_to_email`

### Example CSV

```csv
from_email,password,smtp_host,smtp_port,from_name,user_name,imap_host,imap_port,imap_user_name,imap_password,warmup_enabled,warmup_auto_ramp_up_enabled,warmup_initial_daily_frequency,warmup_ramp_up_frequency,warmup_max_daily_frequency,warmup_tag,inbox_enable,inbox_path,spam_path,pause_cold_emails_when_health_low,pause_cold_emails_health_threshold,sequence_auto_ramp_up_enabled,sequence_initial_daily_frequency,sequence_ramp_up_frequency,sequence_max_daily_frequency,signature_id,custom_tracking_url,dkim_identifier,reply_to_email
john@example.com,secret123,smtp.example.com,465,John Doe,john@example.com,imap.example.com,993,john@example.com,secret123,true,true,5,1,30,warmup,true,INBOX,Spam,true,80,true,30,3,50,6a4b3c2d,track.example.com,default,reply@example.com
```

Create a new inbox placement test to check email deliverability.
Required fields: `name` (min 3 chars), `mode` (`one-time` | `recurring`), and `source` (`from-salesblink` | `from-outside`).
When `source` is `from-salesblink` or `mode` is `recurring`, you must provide `email_senders` (array) or `sender_id` (legacy single sender) and a `content_type` (`custom` | `sequence` | `template`).
- `content_type=custom` requires `subject` and `body`.
- `content_type=sequence` requires `sequence_id` and `template_id`.
